Wachock Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wąchock, Poland

Not demolished. Before this cemetery's establishment, Jews from Wąchock buried their dead in nearby Iłża. Most of the town's 468 Jews recorded in 1921 were murdered at the Treblinka death camp in October 1942; the cemetery's last funerals likely took place in spring 1945, following several attacks on Holocaust survivors. Devastated during and after the war and used as pasture and a landfill, it was restored in 2006 at the initiative of Rafael Faferman, in cooperation with the Poland Jewish Cemetery Restoration Project and city authorities, who fenced 0.16 hectares with a stone wall and unveiled a monument and plaques commemorating the Feferman family and the renovation.
